quotes.quote: Four randomized controlled trials involving 3613 participants met the eligibility criteria.
Rubino’s study randomized participants to either continue with semaglutide or switch to a placebo after reaching the target dose.
O’Neil et al administered a smaller daily dose of semaglutide, ranging from 0.05 mg to 0.4 mg.
Wilding, Rubino, and Wadden conducted their studies over 68 weeks, while O’Neil’s study lasted 52 weeks.

scope.reading: Its 4 trials are STEP 1 (Wilding), STEP 3 (Wadden), STEP 4 (Rubino) and O'Neil 2018 (Table 1, each row bound to its reference). STEP 1 and STEP 3 are the two we pool. STEP 4 is a randomised withdrawal after run-in on semaglutide, and O'Neil 2018 is a 52-week daily dose-ranging trial (0.05 to 0.4 mg) -- both answer different questions from once-weekly 2.4 mg versus placebo from randomisation, so 4 vs 2 is not 2 trials missing from ours.
scope.reported_by: external review of the semaglutide-obesity-weight topic (28 Sep 2026)

method_difference.heading: Different sets, different methods, a coincident number

quotes.quote: mean difference: −11.85%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: −12.81 to − 10.90; P < .00001
a random-effects model was applied a priori for all analyses.

method_difference.reading: Its MD of -11.85 points pools four trials, two of which answer other questions, with RevMan random effects; ours (-11.84) pools STEP 1 and STEP 3 only. The near-identical numbers are a coincidence of different sets and methods, not validation and not an independent result; the two are not the same question.
